reason: Icarus 13.0 returns 0 for $dimensions of the implicit integer localparam in a loop-generate body. IEEE 1800-2023 27.4 and 20.7 require one packed dimension for this predefined integer type. A standalone reproducer returns 0 in Icarus and 1 in Verilator; Celox and Verilator pass the unchanged shared assertions.
Icarus 13.0 cannot bind generate-scope parameters and signals that the block declares after their use ("Unable to bind"). Verilator passes these cases.
Icarus 13.0 resolves a name used before its declaration in the same generate block to the enclosing scope. Verilator (which warns VARHIDDEN) and Celox resolve it to the block's own declaration.

Icarus 13.0 compares a case-generate selector without the common width and signedness of the selector and all labels; IEEE 1800-2023 12.5 makes the comparison unsigned when any operand is unsigned. Verilator agrees with the expected value.

Icarus 13.0 evaluates an input port connection at its self-determined width before padding, losing the carry; IEEE 1800-2023 10.8 and 11.8.2 widen the operands to the port first. Verilator agrees with the expected value.

Icarus 13.0 rejects syntax used by these designs: selects of concatenations and replications (IEEE 1800-2023 A.8.4, primary), keyed and typed assignment patterns, packed-structure parameter declarations, and parameter type declarations in generate blocks.
Icarus 13.0 reports that packed array parameters are not supported, or fails a cast size that depends on a type alias dimension. Verilator passes or reports these four-state cases as unsupported.

Icarus 13.0 reports that unpacked array parameters are not supported (IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.2) and rejects the typed assignment pattern of a struct parameter. Verilator passes the struct-parameter case; its internal error on the $isunbounded array query is recorded separately.
Icarus 13.0 crashes on these designs: a segmentation fault while compiling, or a vvp assertion (vthread.cc of_DISABLE_FLOW) while running. Verilator passes these cases.
Icarus 13.0 evaluates a size query in a generate block with a function from another scope and reaches a $fatal in an active branch. Verilator agrees with the expected value.
Icarus 13.0 rejects a loop-generate condition with unknown bits; Verilator accepts it, and Celox treats an unknown condition as false, as for if-generate (IEEE 1800-2023 12.4, 27.5).
Icarus 13.0 rejects output and inout function arguments (function port is not an input port).
Icarus 13.0 does not distribute an unpacked array connection over the elements of an instance array (IEEE 1800-2023 23.3.3.5) and reports multiple drivers. Verilator passes these cases.
Icarus 13.0 accepts a one-bit '0 connected to a wider port of an instance array, which IEEE 1800-2023 23.3.3.5 makes an error. Verilator rejects it.
Icarus 13.0 does not support inside expressions ("sorry: inside expressions not supported yet"). Verilator passes the case.

Icarus 13.0 returns 2 for $size of an element of a multidimensional packed struct member (value.m[0] of logic [1:0][3:0]); IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 makes it the element's size, 4. Verilator agrees with the expected value.
Icarus 13.0 rejects a data type as the argument of $size ("Type names are not valid expressions here"), which IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 permits. Verilator passes the case.

Icarus 13.0 does not convert a 2-state member of a packed struct with 4-state members from four state when reading it, so a compound assignment to the member keeps X; IEEE 1800-2023 7.2.1 converts it. Verilator cannot check four-state values.
Icarus 13.0 returns the operand of a unary plus unchanged when it has X or Z bits; IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.3 makes the result of an arithmetic operator all X. Verilator cannot check four-state values.

Icarus 13.0 rejects a further select after a runtime index into a multidimensional packed array, or after runtime indices into an unpacked array of them (t[k][j], t[k][2:1], u[j][k][i]: "Array index expressions must be constant here"). Verilator passes the two-state case; the four-state one is outside what it checks.

Icarus 13.0 flattens an out-of-range inner index of a multidimensional packed array into the neighbouring element: a read gives a known value instead of X, and a write lands in that element; IEEE 1800-2023 7.4.6 and 11.5.1 make the select out of range. Verilator cannot check four-state values, and it truncates out-of-range packed indices.
Icarus 13.0 reports that subroutine ports with unpacked dimensions are not yet supported. Verilator passes the valid case.

Icarus 13.0 reports that an assignment pattern with unpacked array items assigned to a multidimensional unpacked array is not yet supported ("Procedural assignment of array or array slice"), so the run cannot count it as a language rejection. The design is invalid (IEEE 1800-2023 7.6, 10.8).

Icarus 13.0 zero-pads a value wider than an explicit field width of %h or %o to the argument's full width (%3h of 32'h1234 prints 00001234); IEEE 1800-2023 21.2.1.2 expands the field to the value without leading zeros (1234). Verilator agrees with the expected value.

Verilator 5.052 is two-state: unknown bits in constant system function arguments ($onehot(2'bx1)) are not kept unknown, so a generate condition differs from IEEE 1800-2023 20.9. Icarus agrees with the expected values.
Verilator 5.052 rejects an x or ? digit in a case-generate label ("no such thing as generate casez"). Icarus passes the case.
Verilator 5.052 does not wrap a self-determined index expression (2'd3 + 2'd1) to its width before selecting; IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 and 11.6.1 make the index 0. Icarus agrees with the expected value.

Verilator 5.052 runs a function call in the right operand of && in a select index when the left operand is false, so its output argument is written; IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.7 does not evaluate that operand. Icarus cannot compile the design (sv_icarus_function_outputs).
Verilator 5.052 fails with an internal error (V3DfgSynthesize: Non-ReadOnly reference) on output and inout function arguments.

Verilator 5.052 rejects a generate block named like a port with an "Unsupported" diagnostic instead of a duplicate-name error, so the run cannot count it as a language rejection. The design is invalid (IEEE 1800-2023 5.6.1, 23.9) and Icarus rejects it as a duplicate declaration.

Verilator 5.052 writes the out-of-range bit of a partially out-of-range indexed part-select (minus_write[i -: 2] with i = 0) into bit 7 instead of discarding it; IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 ignores writes to out-of-range bits. Icarus agrees with the expected value.

Verilator 5.052 rejects an unpacked array argument or assignment pattern item with a narrower element type through "EXTEND unexpected in assignment to unpacked array" (EXTENDS for a signed element), a diagnostic about its own width extension rather than the element types, so the run cannot count it as a language rejection. The designs are invalid (IEEE 1800-2023 7.6, 10.8).

Icarus 13.0 rejects interface port declarations (syntax error in port declarations), modport function imports ("sorry: modport task/function ports are not yet supported") and multidimensional interface instance arrays ("sorry: Multi-dimensional arrays of instances are not yet supported"). Verilator passes these cases.

Verilator 5.052 rejects a four-bit actual connected to a 2x2 interface instance array with scalar ports, requiring only 1 or 2 bits instead of 1 or 4. IEEE 1800-2023 23.3.3.5 distributes packed actuals across all instance dimensions, rightmost dimension first. Celox passes the unchanged shared assertions; Icarus separately rejects multidimensional instance arrays.

Icarus 13.0 rejects unpacked actuals distributed across interface instances (Array inputs needs an array index), aborts on interface array ports (assertion prts.size()==1), and rejects multidimensional instance arrays explicitly. IEEE 1800-2023 23.3.3.5 permits these connections. Verilator passes both unpacked cases; Celox passes all three.

Icarus 13.0 rejects data type arguments to $dimensions: chandle produces a syntax error; parameter and built-in type arguments produce "Type names are not valid expressions here", followed by an assertion for a multidimensional cast. IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 permits these queries. Verilator passes the integral/string/real type case.
Verilator 5.052 returns 1 for $dimensions(chandle). IEEE 1800-2023 6.14 and 20.7 make a chandle a nonarray pointer type, not an integral bit vector, so the expected result is 0.

Icarus 13.0 rejects fixed-size array queries in localparams (a reference to mem is not allowed in a constant expression) and query operands naming typedefs (Type names are not valid expressions here). IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 permits both. Verilator passes the case.

Icarus 13.0 aborts on a runtime array-query dimension (vpiBinaryConst::vpi_get: get 83 not supported). A standalone integer-dimension reproducer instead reports that $left expects an array and optionally an integer. IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 permits a runtime expression selecting a fixed-size dimension.

Icarus 13.0 discards immediate cover pass statements, including with -gassertions. IEEE 1800-2023 16.3 requires the pass statement to execute when the condition is true. Verilator passes when --coverage-user is enabled by the adapter.
Icarus 13.0 rejects subroutine arguments with unpacked dimensions and passing an array to those arguments. IEEE 1800-2023 13.5 permits unpacked subroutine arguments. Verilator passes the case.

Icarus 13.0 returns 0 for $dimensions of package functions returning multidimensional packed values and named/defaulted integral function calls. IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 requires the declared return rank. Verilator passes these cases.

Icarus 13.0 reports 0 for one-bit vector operands of $dimensions, including sized literals, one-bit vector parameters and signing conversions. IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.2, 6.24.1 and 20.7 require vector rank 1; Slang 12.0.0 corroborates these type shapes.

Verilator 5.052 reports 0 for one-bit vector operands of $dimensions, including sized literals and signing conversions. IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.2, 6.24.1 and 20.7 require vector rank 1; Slang 12.0.0 corroborates these type shapes.

Icarus 13.0 rejects parameters initialized to the symbolic value $ and cannot evaluate $isunbounded on bounded parameters in constant expressions. IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.7 permits $ parameter values and 20.6.3 defines the one-bit query result. Slang accepts the cases; Verilator passes integer-parameter declarations, aliases and bounded queries, while scalar unbounded declarations have a separate recorded limitation.

Verilator 5.052 rejects $ and a parameter whose value is $ as an instance parameter override (UNSUPPORTED / cannot convert defparam value to constant). IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.7 permits assigning the symbolic value to another parameter. Slang accepts all four instances and preserves the unbounded value.

Verilator 5.052 raises an internal error in V3EmitCConstInit.h for $isunbounded on an unpacked array parameter. IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.2 permits aggregate value parameters, and 20.6.3 returns false when the parameter is not $. Slang accepts the case and evaluates QUERY to 1'b0.

Verilator 5.052 rejects $ assigned to scalar logic parameters in procedural blocks (UNSUPPORTED: Unbounded outside of queue or string operations). IEEE 1800-2023 6.20.7 permits $ for simple bit vector parameter types, including logic (6.11.1). Slang accepts both cases.

Verilator 5.052 cannot evaluate $timeprecision in a parameter initializer. IEEE 1800-2023 11.2.1 lists the timescale system functions in 20.4 among constant system function calls with constant arguments; this case uses no arguments. Slang 12.0.0 also rejects both timescale functions in constant expressions.

Verilator 5.052 parses $unit only as the start of a qualified name and rejects $timeunit($unit). IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 explicitly accepts $unit and $root as standalone query arguments; Slang in SV 2023 mode accepts this source.

Verilator 5.052 ignores the design-element argument of $timeunit and returns the caller module unit, while $timeprecision returns the design-wide minimum even in a package function. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 requires the selected/current design element scale. A standalone probe with own, child, leaf and package scales reproduces the disagreement without the suite testbench; Slang accepts the sources in SV 2023 mode.

Icarus 13.0 does not implement the SV 2023 $timeunit/$timeprecision functions: it rejects their syntax, cannot synthesize calls, or cannot evaluate parameter initializers. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 defines the queries and 11.2.1 permits constant timescale calls with constant arguments.

Icarus 13.0 compiles procedural and package calls of the SV 2023 timescale functions but vvp exits with errors that $timeunit/$timeprecision are not defined. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 defines both functions; Slang accepts this source in SV 2023 mode.

Icarus 13.0 rejects repeated initial timeunit/timeprecision declarations before the other precision/unit is first declared, reporting a missing precision or missing initial declaration. IEEE 1800-2023 3.14.2.2 permits matching repeats and separate unit/precision declarations before non-time items. Slang 12.0.0 accepts the time declarations (it separately rejects the constant timescale queries).

Verilator 5.052 merges module and package identifiers, warns MODDUP and then cannot find P for a P:: reference. Icarus 13.0 rejects a module declaration that follows a same-named package. IEEE 1800-2023 3.13 gives definitions and packages separate global namespaces; Slang 12.0.0 accepts both declaration orders in this fixture.

Verilator 5.052 ignores bare package arguments of $timeunit/$timeprecision and returns the caller unit/global precision. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 requires the selected design element scale; 3.13 gives packages and definitions separate namespaces. A standalone probe reproduces the wrong package and instance results. Slang 12.0.0 also rejects bare package query arguments, including a package without a same-named module.

Icarus 13.0 rejects standalone $unit arguments of the SV 2023 timescale queries, interface ports and modport function imports. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 requires the interface declaration scope for unqualified calls and accepts $unit/$root arguments; this case also checks cross-file interface copies and unused-interface precision. Slang 12.0.0 in SV 2023 mode accepts the source.

Verilator 5.052 rejects the standalone $root argument of $timeprecision, expecting a dotted hierarchical name. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 explicitly accepts $root and returns the global simulation time unit. Slang 12.0.0 accepts the argument syntax but separately rejects the constant timescale initializers in this type-specialization case.

Icarus 13.0 checks the first digit of timeunit/timeprecision literals and rejects leading-zero integer or fixed-point spellings whose numeric magnitudes are 1, 10 or 100. IEEE 1800-2023 5.8 permits integer/fixed-point time literals, and 3.14.2.2 permits their use in time declarations. A standalone declaration without queries reproduces the failure; Verilator and Slang 12.0.0 accept these declarations.

Verilator 5.052 ignores an interface-instance operand of $timeunit: the Top caller has unit 1ms and returns -3 for i, whose interface declares 100ns and requires -7. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.1 queries the selected design element; 25.3 defines hierarchical interface instances and interface ports. Slang 12.0.0 also reports ExpectedModuleName for interface-instance query arguments.

Icarus 13.0 rejects the typed and generic interface port declarations in this timescale-query case with syntax errors in port declarations. IEEE 1800-2023 25.3 permits these interface ports; 20.4.1 selects the queried design element time scope. The case retains its assertions for direct instances, typed/modport ports, differently bound generic ports and local generate handles.
Verilator 5.052 rejects standalone $unit and $root operands of $printtimescale, expecting :: and a dotted hierarchy respectively. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.2 explicitly accepts both special scope operands.

Verilator 5.052 prints the Top caller scale for a package operand of $printtimescale, reports 1ps instead of the declared 10ps precision inside the package procedure, and omits the required parentheses around the design element name. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.2 selects the queried/current design element and specifies the display format; 3.14.2.3 preserves its declared precision.

Icarus 13.0 rejects standalone $unit and bare package operands of $printtimescale with syntax errors. IEEE 1800-2023 20.4.2 accepts a design element argument and explicitly includes $unit and $root. The shared assertions retain their standard output and precision.

Verilator 5.052 binds the default b=a to the earlier formal a and returns 22 for f(.a(2)) when the enclosing module a is 5. IEEE 1800-2023 13.5.3 evaluates defaults in the scope containing the subroutine declaration, requiring 25. Celox passes all five backend variants.

Icarus 13.0 requires function port defaults to be constant expressions and rejects a reference to a net or variable. IEEE 1800-2023 13.5.3 evaluates a used default in the enclosing declaration scope on each call; the shared case retains its dynamic module-signal default.

Icarus 13.0 returns 1 for $unpacked_dimensions(a[0]) when a is declared logic [7:0] a [0:1]. The selected element has no unpacked dimensions, so IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 requires 0. This four-state case is outside the Verilator adapter.

Icarus 13.0 rejects $unpacked_dimensions of a partially selected multidimensional array ("needs 2 indices, but got only 1") and of an unpacked array slice ("Array cannot be indexed by a range"). IEEE 1800-2023 20.7 permits querying the remaining array type. Verilator passes the case.

Icarus 13.0 reports a syntax error when a local variable declared after a wildcard import has the same name as an unpacked typedef in the package. IEEE 1800-2023 26.3 gives local declarations precedence over potentially visible wildcard imports. Verilator passes the case.

Verilator 5.052 zero-extends int'{default: 1} to a 64-bit parameter (0x00000000ffffffff). IEEE 1800-2023 10.9 gives the expression the self-determined int type, signed under 6.11.3; 6.20.2 requires assignment conversion to the parameter, giving 0xffffffffffffffff. The same Verilator probe sign-extends through an int variable or explicit int cast.

Icarus 13.0 rejects both packed array parameter declarations before the X/Z-index regression can execute. IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 requires sized X results for unknown indices of four-state operands and zero for two-state operands. Verilator cannot validate this case's four-state expectations.

Verilator 5.052 treats a zero $urandom seed as an entropy request, so reseeding with zero does not reproduce the sequence. IEEE 1800-2023 18.13.1 permits any integral seed and requires the same sequence for the same seed. A standalone run reports zero_seed_repeat=0 in Verilator and 1 in Icarus; nonzero seeding repeats in both.

Verilator 5.052 uses the host thread/context RNG for $urandom, so separately seeded design processes interfere when clocked independently. IEEE 1800-2023 18.14.1-2 requires a separate stream per SystemVerilog process, independent of thread execution order. The shared case seeds two module-instance processes identically and compares their streams after alternating activations.

Verilator 5.052 moves an unseeded $urandom draw before the preceding seeded call when optimizing the clocked body, breaking the reseeded reference sequence. Its generated C++ assigns second from VL_RANDOM_I before the preceding VL_URANDOM_SEEDED_II call. IEEE 1800-2023 18.13.1 requires the seed to determine the following stream; 18.14.2 localizes its state to the calling process. The original sequential assertions, short circuits and indexed draw are preserved.

Icarus 13.0 requires the $urandom seed to be a writable integer/time variable or register and terminates simulation for a constant or input-net operand. IEEE 1800-2023 18.13.1 accepts any integral expression and gives a literal seed as an example. A standalone literal-seed probe compiles but vvp exits with the seed-must-be-a-variable error; variable seeds reproduce their streams.

Icarus 13.0 terminates for an 8-bit $urandom seed variable with 'seed variable is less than 32 bits (8)'. IEEE 1800-2023 18.13.1 accepts any integral expression, converted to the int seed formal. A standalone signed/unsigned 8-bit seed probe compiles, then vvp exits with this width error; Verilator passes the same nonzero-seed extension checks.

Verilator 5.052 does not compute $random with the Annex N algorithm: seeding with 0 returns 1631467331 instead of 303379748, and an unseeded $random draws from its own RNG. IEEE 1800-2023 20.14.1 and Annex N define $random as rtl_dist_uniform(seed, LONG_MIN, LONG_MAX) so that implementations repeat the same values. A standalone probe prints the Annex N sequence in Icarus 13.0 and different values in Verilator.

Icarus 13.0 rejects hierarchical interface parameter references in constant declarations, including localparam initializers and port dimensions. Celox and Verilator 5.052 pass the dependent declarations and subsequent instance overrides.

Icarus 13.0 returns 0 for $dimensions of a packed structure field, both through an interface member and through a local structure shadowing the interface handle. Celox and Verilator 5.052 return the declared packed dimension count, consistent with IEEE 1800-2023 20.7. The shared cases also check $size and lexical name resolution.

Verilator 5.052 evaluates an always_comb that reads $time again when the clocking event of the suite testbench fires, although no variable it reads has changed: at 3 ns y is 3 instead of 0. IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2.1 makes always_comb sensitive to the variables it reads, and $time (20.3.1) is none. A standalone probe prints y=0 in Icarus 13.0 and Verilator without a clocking block, and y=3 in Verilator with one.

Icarus 13.0 shares an unpacked local array across overlapping calls of an automatic task, including with an explicit automatic declaration. IEEE 1800-2023 13.3.1 and 13.3.2 require separate storage for each activation. The first call returns 31 instead of 11 after the second call overwrites its array; scalar task locals remain independent.

Icarus 13.0 wakes a process that writes an operand of an event expression and then waits on it (a = 1; @(a ^ b);). IEEE 1800-2023 9.4.2 synchronizes the statement with a value change of the expression; the write happened before the event control executed. Verilator 5.052 agrees with the expected value.

Verilator 5.052 rejects @* in an initial forever ("Unsupported: Event control with implicit sensitivity (@*) in this context"), which IEEE 1800-2023 9.4.2.2 permits in any procedural timing control statement. Icarus 13.0 passes the case.

$dist_uniform with longint or shortint seed variables generates C++ that passes cast temporaries to VL_DIST_UNIFORM(IData&); compilation fails because a non-const lvalue reference cannot bind to an rvalue. IEEE 1800-2023 20.14.2 permits an integral seed variable. Celox passes the unchanged width-conversion case.

Icarus rejects the shortint seed at startup with "$dist_uniform's seed must be an integer/time variable or a register." IEEE 1800-2023 20.14.2 permits an integral seed variable; shortint is integral. Celox passes the unchanged width-conversion case.

Icarus 13.0 rejects std::randomize calls with syntax errors before executing the testbench. IEEE 1800-2023 18.12 defines scope randomization of variables without requiring a class. Verilator executes both the arbitrary-width and control-flow regressions successfully.
